Resolves #18968

Keyboard focus on a grid framed the whole scroll viewport with a 2px ring, including the empty space below the records. An editor handing focus back to the View got the browser's own `auto` ring around the viewport in the same way, because that focus carries no modality stamp. Neither is painted by default any more. The selected cell, row or column, or an open editor, shows where focus is. `--grid-view-focus-outline` still frames keyboard focus when an app sets it, and never pointer focus. The change is one stylesheet, and it removes a rule: the pointer-only `outline: none` is now covered by the base `:focus` rule.

Evidence: L2 (e2e, real Chromium, computed outline on the grid-cell-editing fixture, themes rebuilt from this head) → L2 required (a stylesheet default is only visible in a rendered page). Residual: keyboard focus with nothing selected shows no cue. That state is reachable only by clicking the selected cell again, which clears the selection, and then pressing a key that does not navigate. Any arrow key selects a cell. An app that needs a frame there sets the hook.

## AC Evidence

| AC-1 | `e2e/grid/GridViewFocusOutline.spec.mjs` › *keyboard navigation paints no ring around the View; the selected cell shows where focus is*, and › *an editor handing focus back paints no ring, whether it was cancelled or completed*: Escape, and Tab past the last editable cell, both return focus to the View with `outline-style: none`. Both arms are RED on `dev`'s stylesheet |
| AC-2 | the same arms: the View holds focus and ArrowRight moves the selection to the next cell. The Tab arm ends the edit on the View. `CellEditingTab` and the rest of `e2e/grid` stay green (below) |
| AC-3 | the change touches only `.neo-grid-view`; the first arm asserts the selected cell moved with the keyboard, so the selection cue is what remains |
| AC-4 | › *`--grid-view-focus-outline` frames keyboard focus, and never pointer focus*: with the property set to `3px solid red`, pointer focus has no outline and keyboard focus has exactly that one. Green on `dev` too, as the compatibility control |
| AC-5 | the rule lives in `resources/scss/src/grid/View.scss`, which all five themes (neo light/dark, light, dark, cyberpunk) compile alike. No theme sets the property or styles `.neo-grid-view`. The Brain-gated `GridViewFocus.spec.mjs` (ownership + modality) had pinned the old keyboard ring; its assertion now expects none. It needs the external runtime, so it did not run here |

## Deltas from ticket

- **The browser's own ring.** Measured before writing: after Escape cancels an edit, the View has focus with neither modality class, and Chromium paints `auto 1px rgb(153, 200, 255)` around the whole viewport. So the base `:focus` rule clears every View outline, and the keyboard rule applies only the hook.
- **Where focus shows without the frame**, measured on the fixture: every navigation key leaves a selected cell, starting from the first record if nothing was selected. See the residual above for the only exception.
